page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv7 series, running under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features a 64-bit ARM architecture supplying 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration does not include discrete GPUs or specialized hardware accelerators.

Storage capabilities are highlighted by an integrated 2,835 GB local NVMe SSD array for high-speed ephemeral data handling. In addition to bundled high-capacity local storage, the instance is capable of attaching Premium Storage tiers. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided with the instance.

From an efficiency perspective, the 48-core ARM profile provides high core density and balanced memory capacity suited for scaled horizontal and vertical multi-threaded services. The inclusion of substantial local NVMe storage eliminates the latency penalties of network storage for intermediate data structures, though target software stacks must be compiled natively for the ARM64 instruction set.

The D48pds_v7 is structured for workloads demanding balanced computational throughput and fast disk access, including relational database engines, search indexers, distributed caching clusters, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving applications.
description: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v7 is an ARM64 general-purpose virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Hardware resources include a bundled 2,835 GB local NVMe SSD and support for Premium Storage, while excluding graphics accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The deployment of high-density ARM cores together with low-latency local NVMe capacity provides cost-effective throughput for multi-threaded services, provided environments are compatible with ARM64 instructions. The D48pds_v7 is designed for data-intensive and concurrent workloads such as transactional databases, caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, and distributed application hosting.
